issues.failure_explanation: From |x| >= ||h\lambda| - rad(V_{h\lambda})| the proof infers \int_{V_{h\lambda}} |x|^p d\mu >= ||h\lambda|^p - rad^p| \mu(V_{h\lambda}), but (a-b)^p <= a^p - b^p for a >= b >= 0, p >= 1, so this inference is invalid, and item (i) is false. Counterexample: d=1, \Lambda = Z, h=1, p=2, disjoint cells with V_0 = [-1/2,1/2), \mu = \delta_{-1/2}. Then -1/2 lies in V_{-1}, so the left side of (i) is |-1|^2 = 1 while the right side is rad(V_0)^2 + M_2(\mu) = 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2. The valid estimate, from |h\lambda| <= |x| + rad(V_{h\lambda}), is \sum |h\lambda|^p \mu(V_{h\lambda}) <= 2^{p-1}(M_p(\mu) + h^p rad(V_0)^p).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side of (i) by 2^{p-1}(M_p(\mu) + h^p rad(V_0)^p) and adjust the two citing moment computations accordingly; no theorem statement, rate, or guarantee changes.
issues.overall_effect: Item (i) is false as stated; the moment-finiteness computations in Theorems THM:InfiniteLatticeDirac and THM:LatticePiecewiseConstant quote it, so those displayed bounds are wrong as written, although the theorems' conclusions (membership in W_p and the O(h) rates) remain valid with the corrected constant.
issues.title: Radial sum estimate in Lemma LEM:RadialEstimates (i) is false (missing factor 2^{p-1})
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line constant insertion proved by the standard (a+b)^p <= 2^{p-1}(a^p+b^p) argument; every advertised conclusion and rate survives unchanged, only intermediate moment-estimate constants move.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $N\in\N$ be fixed, $\mc{N}=\mc{N}(B_R,V_0)$, and set $h=3\left(\frac{\mc{N}}{N}\right)^{\frac1d}$. Then $\mu_h = \sum_{\lambda\in \Lambda} \mu(V_{h\lambda})\delta_{h\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation of $\mu$

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma LEM:CoveringNumber justifies only the second inequality. The first, that the number of h\Lambda-cells meeting supp(\mu) is at most \mc N(B_R, hV_0), is false in general: the translates in the definition of \mc N are arbitrary, and one translate of hV_0 can meet several lattice cells (e.g. a tiny ball centered at a corner where four cells of hZ^2 meet is covered by one translate of hV_0 but meets four cells). Since the cells meeting B_R themselves cover B_R, the valid bounds are \mc N(B_R,hV_0) <= #{cells meeting B_R} <= 3^d \mc N(B_R,hV_0), so an unaccounted factor up to 3^d appears. Moreover h = 3(\mc N/N)^{1/d} exceeds 1 whenever N < 3^d \mc N, leaving the h in (0,1] hypotheses of Theorem THM:InfiniteLatticeDirac and of the second inequality of Lemma LEM:CoveringNumber; in that regime the stated guarantee fails outright: d=2, \Lambda = Z^2, \mu = normalized Lebesgue measure on B((1.5,1.5), 0.01), R = 0.02 (so \mc N = 1), N = 1 gives h = 3 and a \mu_h with 4 atoms, contradicting 'at most N-term'.

failure_location.quote: Note that for any $h\in(0,1]$, $\mu_h$ has at most \[\mc{N}(B_R,hV_{0}) \leq 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}(B_R,V_0) = 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert a packing bound #{cells meeting B_R} <= 3^d \mc N(B_R, hV_0), re-optimize with h = 9(\mc N/N)^{1/d} (the constant 3 becomes 9 in the final estimate), and either assume N >= 9^d \mc N so that h <= 1 or treat h > 1 separately; the O(N^{-1/d}) rate with at most N terms is preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The 'at most N-term' guarantee of Theorem THM:NTermDirac is unproved and is false in some regimes; the term count of Corollary COR:NTermPiecewiseConstant, whose proof mimics this one, inherits the defect. The W_p rate bound itself (it equals rad(V_0) h) is unaffected.
issues.title: Term count in Theorem THM:NTermDirac is not bounded by the covering number and can exceed N
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a new (short) counting lemma, a worse constant, and an extra hypothesis or case for small N: a contained argument and limited weakening that keep the advertised rate and scope, hence more than a local patch but no new global architecture or rate loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Setting $h=N^{-\frac1d}$ yields $N$ cubes of length $N^{-\frac1d}$ in the unit cube, so appealing to the proof of Theorem \ref{THM:InfiniteLatticeDirac} yields the desired rate upon noticing that $\rad([-\frac12,\frac12]^d) = \frac{\sqrt{d}}{2}$ and $\mathcal{N}([-\frac12,\frac12]^d,[-\frac12,\frac12]^d) = 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: With \Lambda_N = (N^{-1/d} Z)^d the cells are centered at lattice points, and the cells meeting the open unit cube include a boundary layer: writing m = N^{1/d} (assuming it integral), each coordinate range admits m+1 cells when m is even, so up to (m+1)^d cells can carry mass. E.g. d=2, N=4 (h=1/2): the cells (k/2 - 1/4, k/2 + 1/4] with k in {-1,0,1} in each axis all meet (-1/2,1/2)^2, so \mu_N can have 9 atoms, not at most 4 (the support may approach the boundary since only containment in the interior is assumed). If N is not a perfect d-th power, 'N cubes of length N^{-1/d} in the unit cube' is not realizable at all. The W_p bound (sqrt d / 2) N^{-1/d} is correct; only the term count fails.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the half-cell shifted lattice so the Voronoi cells align with the faces of [-1/2,1/2]^d (the 'shifted Voronoi regions' of the surrounding prose) and take N = m^d, or weaken the conclusion to at most (ceil(N^{1/d})+1)^d terms; the rate and constant are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The 'at most N-term' guarantees of Corollaries COR:NpixelDirac and COR:NpixelIndicator are false as stated for even m = N^{1/d} and not meaningful for non-perfect d-th powers; the stated convergence-rate bounds still hold.
issues.title: Corollary COR:NpixelDirac's exact N-cell count fails for the unshifted lattice
issues.why_classification: A one-line construction fix (shift the lattice, or restrict to perfect d-th powers) restores the stated guarantee with identical rate, constant, method, and camera-model interpretation; no new argument or loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $f_\mu(x) \leq \frac{\eps^p}{ 3C \vert x \vert^{p+d+1} }$ where $C$ is the integration constant from integrating over concentric $d$-spheres,

issues.failure_explanation: \int_R^\infty r^{d-1}/r^{d+1} dr = \int_R^\infty r^{-2} dr = 1/R, which is <= 1 only when R >= 1. Hence condition (1) yields I_1 <= \eps^p/(3R), not \eps^p/3, and for small R the theorem is false as stated: take d = p = 1 (so C = 2), R = 1/12, and f_\mu(x) = \eps/(6|x|^3) on {|x| > R} (outside mass 24\eps, feasible for \eps <= 1/24, remaining mass placed at 0; conditions (2) and (3) vacuous). Then I_1 = (\eps/3)(1/R - 1/(2R)) = \eps/(6R) = 2\eps, so W_1(\mu, \hat\mu) >= 2\eps > \eps, contradicting the conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen condition (1) to f_\mu(x) <= \eps^p R / (3C|x|^{p+d+1}) (equivalently, add the hypothesis R >= 1); then I_1 <= \eps^p/3 and the theorem and its corollary hold with unchanged conclusions.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem THM:noncompact_ext is false as stated for R < 1; Corollary cor:added-1 inherits the defect, so its '+ \eps' term is not guaranteed under the stated hypotheses.
issues.title: Absolutely continuous tail condition in Theorem THM:noncompact_ext misses a factor of R
issues.why_classification: The statement is false for a whole regime (R < 1) and the fix rewrites a substantive hypothesis (extra factor R) or excludes small balls: a limited weakening that leaves a recognizably comparable tail-decay result, with no new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The shells are anchored at integers while the cost is measured from R: for j = floor(R) the term (j+1-R)^{-2} = (1-{R})^{-2} is unbounded as the fractional part {R} -> 1, so the displayed bound by \pi^2/6 holds only for integer R. The theorem is false as stated: e.g. d=2, p=1, R=0.9, with \mu_\perp an atomless singular measure of mass m_0 = (\eps/(3(0.1)^3))(6/\pi^2) \approx 203\eps supported on the circle |x|=1 (conditions (1) and (3) vacuous, condition (2) satisfied with equality in the first shell, \eps chosen small so m_0 <= 1). Then I_2 = (1-0.9) m_0 \approx 20\eps > \eps, so W_1(\mu,\hat\mu) > \eps, contradicting the conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-anchor the shells at R: require, for integers j >= 0, \mu_\perp(B_{(R+j, R+j+1]}) <= (\eps^p/(3(j+1)^{p+2}))(6/\pi^2); then I_2 <= \sum_j (j+1)^p \mu_\perp(B_{(R+j,R+j+1]}) <= \eps^p/3 and the theorem holds with the same conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem THM:noncompact_ext is false as stated for every non-integer R; Corollary cor:added-1 inherits the defect.
issues.title: Singular-part shell estimate in Theorem THM:noncompact_ext fails for non-integer R
issues.why_classification: The theorem fails across all non-integer radii and the repair must restate hypothesis (2) with shells based at R rather than at integers: a contained rewriting of a substantive decay condition that preserves the conclusion and the character of the result, so moderate rather than minor or serious.
